{
  "schema_version": "formalization-faithfulness-1",
  "role": "blind-translation",
  "dossier_sha256": "e3531290775fa4a6e71890f258ad43bc90de45417b738ae1923fa4ce97bdcc99",
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "id": "D001",
      "name": "LocalDef001",
      "meaning": "The assertion that advance takes equal values on any two histories whose final states are equal.",
      "effect_on_target": "Expands the left side of the equivalence into a universally quantified implication about pairs of histories.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D002",
      "name": "Eq",
      "meaning": "Equality of two objects of the same type.",
      "effect_on_target": "Compares entire states in the left side and entire functions in the right side. These function equalities can equivalently be expressed pointwise.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D003",
      "name": "Exists",
      "meaning": "Existential quantification over an object satisfying the indicated predicate.",
      "effect_on_target": "Requires one state-to-state function step representing advance on every history.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D004",
      "name": "Fin",
      "meaning": "Fin k is the type of natural-number indices strictly less than k.",
      "effect_on_target": "Histories have indices 0 through n, and each state has component indices 0 through m−1. Fin 0 is empty.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D005",
      "name": "Fin.last",
      "meaning": "Fin.last n is the index with natural-number value n in Fin (n+1).",
      "effect_on_target": "Selects the final entry of each history.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D006",
      "name": "Function.comp",
      "meaning": "Function composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)).",
      "effect_on_target": "The right side states that advance first selects the final state and then applies step.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D007",
      "name": "HAdd.hAdd",
      "meaning": "The addition operation supplied by a heterogeneous-addition instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "With the displayed natural-number instances, computes n+1, the history length.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D008",
      "name": "Iff",
      "meaning": "Logical equivalence, asserting both implications between two propositions.",
      "effect_on_target": "Asserts that final-state invariance and existence of a representing step function imply each other.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D009",
      "name": "Nat",
      "meaning": "The natural numbers, including zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "Both m and n range over all natural numbers without positivity assumptions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D010",
      "name": "OfNat.ofNat",
      "meaning": "The value assigned to a natural-number literal by its OfNat instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets the literal 1 in the history length as the natural number one.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D011",
      "name": "Real",
      "meaning": "The type of real numbers.",
      "effect_on_target": "Each state assigns a real number to every cell and component index. No arithmetic, order, or topology on the reals is used in the proposition.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D012",
      "name": "instAddNat",
      "meaning": "The natural-number addition instance, whose operation is Nat.add.",
      "effect_on_target": "Ensures that the addition in n+1 is ordinary natural-number addition.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D013",
      "name": "instHAdd",
      "meaning": "An instance converting addition on a type into heterogeneous addition with all three types equal.",
      "effect_on_target": "Connects HAdd.hAdd to the natural-number addition instance used in the history length.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D014",
      "name": "instOfNatNat",
      "meaning": "The instance interpreting a natural-number literal as that same natural number.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes the displayed literal 1 exactly one in Nat.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D015",
      "name": "Function.FactorsThrough",
      "meaning": "For functions g : A → C and f : A → B, the proposition that for every a,b in A, f(a)=f(b) implies g(a)=g(b).",
      "effect_on_target": "Requires advance to be constant on each set of histories sharing the same final state; its definition does not itself quantify a representing function.",
      "status": "understood"
    }
  ],
  "translation": {
    "binders": [
      "Cell is an arbitrary type in universe u_1, with no additional structure or nonemptiness assumption.",
      "m is an arbitrary natural number.",
      "n is an arbitrary natural number.",
      "Let S = Cell → Fin m → ℝ be the state space and H = Fin (n+1) → S the history space. advance is an arbitrary function H → S.",
      "On the left side, h and k are universally quantified elements of H.",
      "On the right side, step is existentially quantified with type S → S. It may depend on Cell, m, n, and advance, but the same step must work for every history."
    ],
    "hypotheses": [
      "There are no additional hypotheses on the universally quantified parameters.",
      "Within the left-side condition, the implication assumes h(n)=k(n) as equality of entire states."
    ],
    "conclusions": [
      "The condition ∀ h,k ∈ H, h(n)=k(n) ⇒ advance(h)=advance(k) is equivalent to the existence of step : S → S such that advance = step ∘ (h ↦ h(n)).",
      "Equivalently, the right-side equality requires advance(h)(c)(j)=step(h(n))(c)(j) for every history h, every c ∈ Cell, and every j ∈ Fin m."
    ],
    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "A state s is an arbitrary function assigning a real number s(c)(j) to each cell c and component index j<m.",
      "A history is an arbitrary sequence of n+1 states, indexed by 0,…,n.",
      "The final-state projection p : H → S is p(h)=h(n).",
      "LocalDef001 n advance means ∀ h,k ∈ H, p(h)=p(k) ⇒ advance(h)=advance(k).",
      "Equality of final states means equality at every cell and component; equality of output states has the same meaning."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "For every type of cells, every natural number m of components, every natural number n, and every function advance from histories of n+1 real-valued states to a state, the following are equivalent: any two histories with identical final states have identical outputs under advance; and there exists a function step from states to states such that, for every history, its output under advance equals step applied to its final state."
  },
  "restrictions_and_vacuity_risks": [
    "Histories always have at least one entry because their length is n+1.",
    "If n=0, a history consists solely of its final state. The final-state invariance condition then holds for every advance, and every advance has the stated representation.",
    "If m=0 or Cell is empty, the state space has exactly one element. The history space also has exactly one element, so both sides hold automatically.",
    "Even otherwise, the state and history spaces are nonempty: zero-valued states and constant histories exist. Every state occurs as a final state via a constant history.",
    "The proposition quantifies over all histories of the specified type, without restricting them to histories satisfying an evolution law or other admissibility condition.",
    "No finiteness, geometry, adjacency, or other structure is imposed on Cell.",
    "Dependence only on the final state does not require dependence only on the same cell or component: step may use the entire final state.",
    "The proposition does not impose linearity, continuity, computability, conservation, probabilistic behavior, or any other regularity on advance or step.",
    "The witness is provided separately for each n and advance; no common step across different history lengths is asserted.",
    "Only existence of step is explicitly asserted. Uniqueness follows from surjectivity of the final-state projection, but is not a separate clause of the target."
  ],
  "ambiguities": []
}
